plain: To force or limit what a person can do.

webster.text: In a general sense, to strain; to press; to urge; to drive; to exert force, physical or moral, either in urging to action or in restraining it.

example.quote: For with what ever view it was framed, truth constrains me to say, that it is insiduous in its form, and ruinous in its tendency.
example.cite: Letters of Agrippa I-XI, Massachusetts Gazette, Nov. 1787-Jan. 1788
